classification_meaning.different_structure: Different input/state/output obligations; not a claim of pretraining novelty or statistical independence.
classification_meaning.shared_mechanism: Shared repair mechanism with specified additional obligations; actual minimum patch still needs review.
classification_meaning.near_template: A potentially near-identical minimum repair requires explicit adjudication, not automatic admission.

tasks.mechanics: Expire accepted reservations before sequential admission; equality and rejected-state handling interact.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Change strict expiration to inclusive expiration without changing accepted-only accounting.
tasks.concern: The initial expiration-comparator edit may be a near-template of S01 despite the richer surrounding task.

tasks.mechanics: Project data-only logical addresses across ignored control blocks, preserving zero output positions.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Do not advance logical address for control blocks; retain half-open coverage.

tasks.mechanics: Clip weighted intervals and add their contributions over a bounded integer domain.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Replace discarding partially exterior intervals with correct clipping.

tasks.mechanics: Independent interleaved transaction lifetimes; commit emits, rollback discards, ID reuse resets.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: A new lifetime must not reuse the old ID total, while peer transactions remain intact.
tasks.concern: Actual initial code needs only begin-time assignment of zero to the existing ID slot; legal inputs make retained inactive entries unobservable. C04:S03 is a near-template blocker.

tasks.mechanics: Per-key high-water marks ignore older/duplicate numbers and reset locally on reconnection.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Reset the addressed key high-water state without resetting other keys.

tasks.mechanics: Inner reset clears current sum only; outer delimiter clears sum and peak; empty and negative peaks remain distinct.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Preserve the group's historical peak when resetting the inner running sum.

tasks.mechanics: Sequential multiset orders with all-or-nothing stock changes and empty-order success.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Prevent partial consumption by rejected orders, not merely add per-item deletion.

tasks.mechanics: Count distinct source memberships per label, threshold counts and sort qualifying labels.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Deduplicate within each source, not globally, before accumulating source votes.

tasks.mechanics: Count cross-side equal-value index products excluding same-source pairs.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Retain repeated records as distinct indices instead of set-deduplicating each side.

tasks.mechanics: Refresh existing keys and evict oldest on insertion, returning every eviction and final order.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Move a refreshed resident key to the newest position before future eviction.
tasks.concern: Per-prefix last-occurrence reconstruction is possible; actual repair must not be accepted solely because the output wrapper changed.

tasks.mechanics: All valid votes count, invalid votes set no first-valid position; rank by count then first-valid order.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Do not let invalid votes establish candidate tie order.

tasks.mechanics: Select by priority with per-category quotas, then restore original index order without label deduplication.
tasks.initial_repair_obligation: Consume quotas in priority order rather than original input order.

C01: Confirmed actual minimum repair excludes equality from time membership, just as S01; accepted-only capacity state is already correct and adds no repair obligation.
Both involve endpoint equality, but admission expires a dynamic accepted set rather than computing one interval length.
Expiration removes individual timed reservations, not a delimiter resetting one segment sum.
Capacity occupancy is timed numeric state, not per-row duplicate detection.
Weighted active occupancy and expiry differ from multiset intersection cardinality.
Both admit against resources; C01 releases by time and handles rejected future state rather than consuming one word.
Chronological admission produces per-request booleans, not a single earliest maximum index.
Accepted reservations preserve multiplicity and lifetimes, not first-label deduplication.
C02: Both use boundaries, but C02 repairs logical address advancement around controls rather than a threshold comparison.
Intersection arithmetic is shared; the required repair concerns control-free cumulative addresses and output positions.
Control blocks are skipped addresses, not reset delimiters for independent sums.
Zero-overlap output positions remain; no duplicate set is maintained.
Per-block positional overlap is not a bag-frequency minimum.
Address ranges are not consumed inventory and have no success/failure transaction.
Every data block gets a coverage count rather than selecting a maximum.
Duplicate/empty blocks retain positions rather than being deduplicated.
C03: Bounds are shared, but partially exterior intervals need clipping and accumulated contributions rather than a prefix count.
Clipping uses intersection concepts, but signed weights and many overlapping intervals produce a load vector.
Spatial prefix reconstruction is not delimiter-separated sequence accumulation.
Duplicate intervals add weight instead of making a row nonunique.
Repeated intervals sum signed weights rather than take minimum multiplicities.
Contributions do not consume a finite inventory or admit demand.
All domain positions are returned; there is no chosen maximum index.
Interval duplicates must contribute repeatedly, not retain first labels.
C04: Transaction validity and lifetime resets do not use a numerical cutoff.
Event lifetimes are not interval-overlap lengths.

Confirmed actual minimum repair replaces begin-time setdefault with assignment of zero to this ID slot. Like S03 it resets an old accumulator at a new segment boundary; legal lifecycles make retained inactive entries unobservable, so interleaving/rollback need no additional repair.
Both prevent state leakage across scopes; C04 resets one active ID without clearing interleaved peers.
Amounts are added within transaction lifetimes, not intersected by frequencies.
Rollback affects event-local totals, not availability of consumed characters.
Every commit emits its own total in event order rather than choosing a maximum.
Repeated transaction IDs represent distinct lifetimes and are not deduplicated.
C05: Sequence gaps depend on per-key history and reset, not a sorted-list cutoff.
Missing-number differences use moving high-water marks, not overlap of two static ranges.
Resetting history is shared, but per-key high-water and older-message immunity differ from resetting a segment sum.
Key-local reset resembles scoped state, but keys interleave and high-water ignores stale values instead of tracking row duplicates.
Duplicate messages produce zero gap without counting bag intersections.
History reset does not consume or satisfy multiset demand.
High-water maxima are maintained per key and every event emits a gap, not a single earliest argmax.
Duplicate numbers are ignored only within key lifetimes; output retains every event position.
C06: Two marker lifetimes and prefix peaks do not count values before a cutoff.
Peaks across reset segments are not pairwise interval lengths.
Both process delimiters, but inner reset must preserve peak while outer reset clears it; the required patch is not simply reset total.
Scope-local state is shared, but two reset levels and negative/null peaks differ from row-local seen sets.
Ordered prefix values determine peaks; multiplicity minima do not.
No stock, resource admission or character consumption occurs.
Both involve maxima, but C06 returns values of prefix sums per group with reset semantics, not an earliest index.
Repeated values influence sums and marker state rather than being deduplicated.
C07: All-or-nothing multiset orders do not use a time cutoff.
Order acceptance is not intersection length.
Failed orders preserve prior inventory rather than resetting an accumulator to zero.
Repeated coupons are valid quantities, not row-uniqueness violations.
Multiplicity is shared, but sequential atomic consumption cannot be reduced to one multiset-intersection size.
Closest inventory neighbor; C07 must roll back a partial failure so later orders work, whereas S06 lacks one successful removal.
Input order is fixed and all orders receive decisions; no best score is selected.
Coupon duplicates are essential stock, not repeated labels to discard.
C08: Source-vote thresholding occurs after local deduplication, not a sorted prefix boundary.
Distinct-source membership is not geometric interval overlap.
Per-source deduplication does not reset numeric segment totals.
Both scope duplicate state by inner collection; C08 accumulates one membership vote per source instead of reporting row uniqueness.
Frequency reasoning is shared, but counts are source incidence rather than minimum bag multiplicities.
Membership votes are not depleted when another label qualifies.
All threshold-qualified labels are returned sorted, not one best index.
Deduplication is local to each source, then global counts and ASCII output are required instead of first-encounter output.
C09: Join index counts have no cutoff-order assumption.
Record equality pairs are not interval intersection lengths.
There are no delimiter resets or lifetime totals.
Duplicate records create additional pairs instead of making a row invalid.
Both involve two-sided multiplicity; C09 uses frequency products minus same-source products, not frequency minima.
Records may match many opposing indices and are not consumed after a match.
Every valid pair counts; no priority or argmax selection occurs.
Deduplication is precisely an error because record indices remain distinct.
C10: Capacity and recency updates are not a timestamp cutoff count.
Resident keys and evictions are not interval lengths.
Eviction removes one oldest key; it does not reset the whole sequence state.
Key uniqueness is maintained with movement and eviction, not independently judged within rows.
Resident order is distinct-key state rather than bag intersection counts.
Capacity is a resource, but existing-key refresh changes victim order instead of consuming item multiplicities.
Order determines a victim repeatedly, unlike one earliest maximum with fixed scores.
Both retain distinct keys, but refresh moves keys and affects later evictions; first-label deduplication cannot reproduce the trace.
C11: Validity-gated vote history does not compare times to a cutoff.
Vote totals and tie order are unrelated to interval geometry.
Source boundaries do not reset counts; all valid votes accumulate.
Same-source duplicate valid votes must count rather than invalidate a row.
Repeated votes count, but ranking by totals and first-valid position differs from minimum bag frequencies.
Votes do not consume inventory or depend on demand fulfillment.
Stable tie behavior is shared, but invalid events must not establish position and all candidates are ranked.
First occurrence matters only after validity filtering; duplicate valid votes alter ranking instead of being discarded.
C12: Priority and category quota determine selection, not a time-threshold prefix.
Category capacity is not a range-overlap computation.
Per-category quota decreases rather than resetting sequence totals.
Repeated labels remain distinct record indices, not uniqueness failures.
Category counts constrain selection but do not calculate bag intersections.
Both consume capacity, but record priority, category identity and restored output order control admission.
Priority ties use indices, but multiple category limits and output reordering go beyond choosing one earliest maximum.
Labels are not deduplicated; selected original record indices are preserved and sorted.
